steps.name: QC, sample_01 audit, count-format and ID-space check
caveats: PCA and detection fractions are diagnostics, not a basis for dropping samples in this step.
A 12,000-gene matrix is likely already filtered upstream; do not attempt to recover missing genes.
steps.context: Files: /eval-four-models-v2-without-python-two-group-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 x 13: gene labels + 12 samples, Salmon gene-level counts; record does not state whether length correction was applied) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-python-two-group-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 x 2: one row per sample with condition; condition values expected to be 'treated' = AD lesional and 'control'). Human skin. All scripts Python per user constraint. Known a priori: sample_01 is ~4x below the median library size. Do NOT re-profile the dataset generally; only produce the audit quantities listed in the constraints.
steps.question: Do the 12 sample columns of counts.csv match the 12 condition labels in metadata.csv (6 treated / 6 control), and exactly how shallow is sample_01 (profiled ~4x below the median library size)?
constraints: All scripts in Python (pandas/numpy/scipy/matplotlib/scikit-learn); no R.

Read both CSVs and assert: the 12 sample columns of counts.csv are exactly the 12 sample rows of metadata.csv; the condition column (identify by content if the column name differs) contains exactly the values 'treated' and 'control', 6 of each. Fail loudly on any mismatch.

Per sample report: total counts, ratio of total counts to the cohort median (sample_01 must appear ~4x below), its condition group, and the fraction of the 12,000 genes with counts >= 10. State explicitly which group (treated or control) sample_01 belongs to.

Count-format check: compute the fraction of matrix values that are non-integer (np.floor round-trip). If essentially all values are integer, classify the input as raw counts (valid for pydeseq2). If a material fraction is fractional, classify it as Salmon length-corrected/scaled counts and flag it: downstream count-model DE is then approximate, and the caveat must be carried into T1S2/T1S3 reports.

ID-space check: classify the row labels as HGNC symbols vs Ensembl (ENSG) vs Entrez numeric, report the dominant class with examples, and persist the mapping need for T2S1 (NCBI human gene-identifier table in the reference data if mapping is required).

PCA for diagnostics only: log1p(counts/total*1e6), z-score genes, 2 components, scatter PC1-PC2 colored by condition with sample_01 labeled; report whether sample_01 is an extreme point and whether the two groups separate.
Do NOT exclude, down-weight, or modify any sample in this step — quantify only.
Outputs: qc_samples.csv (per-sample totals, ratios, detection fractions), qc_report.md, pca.png.
steps.description: Audit of the 12 samples: condition agreement, sample_01 depth quantification, raw-vs-length-corrected count verdict, ID-space classification, diagnostic PCA.
acceptance_criteria: qc_report.md states sample_01's group, its total-count ratio to the median, and a raw-vs-scaled verdict on the count matrix with the measured non-integer fraction.
The counts/metadata sample set is asserted equal (no silent join drops).
PCA plot shows all 12 points, colored by condition, with sample_01 annotated.
ID space of the 12,000 row labels is reported with examples.

steps.name: DE: treated vs control, all 12 samples
caveats: pydeseq2 contrast naming is data-dependent (level names from the metadata); confirm the coefficient rather than hard-coding it from memory of the values.
With n=6 per group, expect modest power: report effect sizes (shrunken LFC) alongside significance; do not over-interpret the tail of the pvalue distribution.
steps.context: Uses the full 12,000 x 12 count matrix (counts.csv) and the verified condition labels (metadata.csv; 'treated' = AD lesional, 'control'). T1S1 provides the count-format verdict, sample_01's group, and the ID space. Python-only per user constraint: use pydeseq2, which implements the DESeq2 median-of-ratios / NB-Wald workflow; its size factors will down-weight the shallow sample_01's library size, but the definitive robustness test is T1S3. No network; no R.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between AD lesional (treated, n=6) and control (n=6) skin using all 12 samples, with LFC shrinkage and FDR control?
constraints: All scripts in Python (pydeseq2); no R.

Build the design with condition as a categorical factor and 'control' as the reference level so that positive log2FoldChange means higher in treated (AD lesional). Verify the fitted coefficient/contrast name and the sign convention from the results object before trusting any LFC; report which coefficient was used.
Run the full pydeseq2 pipeline (size factors, dispersion, Wald test) on all 12 samples, and compute shrunk LFCs (apeglm shrinkage); report both raw and shrunk log2FoldChange.
Multiple testing: Benjamini-Hochberg; count and report genes at padj < 0.05 (primary) and padj < 0.1 (secondary), in both directions.

Persist the complete 12,000-row results table de_full.csv: gene id, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, shrunk_log2FoldChange. Also persist the ranked gene list for T2S1 (all genes ranked by sign(shrunk_log2FoldChange) * log10(1 + 1/pvalue), no ties broken by dropping); document the exact ranking metric in the step report.
Report sample_01's fitted size factor. If T1S1 flagged the matrix as length-corrected/non-integer, carry that caveat verbatim into the results report (DE is approximate under that input).

Sanity check before reporting: housekeeping genes (e.g., GAPDH, ACTB, HPRT1 if present) should not be among the top |LFC| hits; if zero genes pass padj < 0.05, report the smallest pvalue and its gene instead of silently passing.
Outputs: de_full.csv, ranked_list_full.tsv (gene, rank_score), volcano plot, top-10 up and top-10 down table, de_report.md.
steps.description: Primary differential-expression result: pydeseq2 (DESeq2-style NB Wald) treated vs control on all 12 samples, shrunk LFCs, BH FDR, full ranked table for downstream enrichment.
acceptance_criteria: de_full.csv contains all 12,000 genes with baseMean, raw and shrunk LFC, pvalue, padj.
The contrast direction is verified (positive LFC = up in treated) and stated in de_report.md.
DE gene counts at padj < 0.05 and padj < 0.1 are reported for both directions, plus sample_01's size factor.

steps.name: Sensitivity: re-run DE without shallow sample_01
caveats: Do not change any pipeline setting between runs — only the sample set may differ, or the comparison is confounded.
An unbalanced 5-vs-6 design is fine for a sensitivity check; report the actual group sizes, do not drop more samples to re-balance.
steps.context: T1S1 established sample_01's condition group and depth deficit (~4x below the median library size); T1S2 produced de_full.csv and the full ranked list. Because a ~5x-shallow library has sparse per-gene counts that can inflate gene-wise dispersion in the NB model, leaving sample_01 out and comparing is the decisive robustness test for the shallow-sample concern. Groups will be unbalanced (5 vs 6) if sample_01 is in one arm — report the resulting group sizes. Python-only.
steps.question: How much of the treated-vs-control differential expression depends on the shallow sample_01, and which genes remain significant without it?
constraints: All scripts in Python (pydeseq2); no R.

Re-run the IDENTICAL pydeseq2 pipeline (same size-factor method, same dispersion, same contrast with 'control' as reference, same apeglm shrinkage, same BH FDR) on the 11 samples excluding sample_01. Persist de_reduced.csv in the same schema as de_full.csv and a reduced ranked list ranked_list_reduced.tsv with the same ranking metric as T1S2.

Comparison, reported with numbers: (a) Spearman correlation of shrunk log2FoldChange between the full and reduced runs across all genes; (b) Jaccard overlap of DE gene sets at padj < 0.05 (both directions); (c) explicit lists of genes DE in the full run but NOT in the reduced run (sample_01-dependent) and the reverse (emergent without sample_01); (d) the top-10 |shrunken LFC| set in each run and how many differ.

Produce de_robust.csv: the full-run table with an added boolean column significant_without_sample_01 (DE at padj < 0.05 in the reduced run) and a flag column sample_01_dependent (DE only in the full run).

Decision rule to state in the report: if >20% of full-run DE genes (padj < 0.05) drop out, or the top-10 |LFC| sets differ in >3 genes, the headline conclusions must rest on the reduced run and the affected genes must be flagged sample_01_dependent; otherwise the full-run result is robust to the shallow sample. Say which case applied.
Outputs: de_reduced.csv, ranked_list_reduced.tsv, de_robust.csv, comparison table, sensitivity_report.md with the decision.
steps.description: Leave-one-out (shallow sample) sensitivity analysis: identical pydeseq2 pipeline on 11 samples, quantitative comparison to the full run, and a flagged robust DE table.
acceptance_criteria: de_reduced.csv covers all 12,000 genes from the 11-sample run, same schema as de_full.csv.
The report contains the Spearman correlation, Jaccard overlap, both difference lists, and the explicit decision-rule verdict on sample_01 dependence.
de_robust.csv carries the significant_without_sample_01 and sample_01_dependent flags for every gene.

steps.name: HALLMARK GSEA + ORA on the DE signature
caveats: HALLMARK sets are HGNC symbols — running them against Ensembl ids fails silently as an empty match; the ID-space check from T1S1 must gate the join.
FDR < 0.25 is the conventional GSEA threshold; do not silently tighten it, but do state it.
With 50 sets the multiple-testing burden is light, but the leading-edge (not whole-set) membership should be shown so the reported biology is not an artifact of a few genes.
steps.context: Inputs: ranked_list_full.tsv and de_full.csv from T1S2 (primary), ranked_list_reduced.tsv, de_reduced.csv and de_robust.csv from T1S3. Reference data (resolve via the environment's reference catalog, e.g. query 'hallmark'): the MSigDB human hallmark collection — 50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols. If the T1S1 ID-space check found the matrix labeled by Ensembl or Entrez ids, map to HGNC symbols with the NCBI human gene-identifier table in the reference data (Symbol column; Ensembl cross-references in the dbXrefs field) and report mapping coverage for the 12,000 genes and for the DE genes. No network; the GMT and ID table must come from the provisioned reference data. Python-only per user constraint.
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB human HALLMARK pathways are enriched in the AD lesional vs control signature, in the full (n=12) and the shallow-sample-excluded (n=11) runs?
constraints: All scripts in Python (gseapy); no R.

Pre-ranked GSEA with gseapy.prerank (fgsea-style permutation) on both ranked lists against the 50 human HALLMARK sets; rank metric as documented by T1S2/T1S3 (sign of shrunken LFC x log10(1+1/p)). Significance threshold: BH FDR < 0.25. Report NES, nominal p, FDR, and leading-edge genes for the top 10 sets per run.

Over-representation analysis (hypergeometric, BH-corrected) of DE genes (padj < 0.05) from de_robust.csv against the background of all 12,000 genes in the assay; report top hits separately for up and down genes.

Concordance: for the sets significant in at least one run, report the NES correlation between the two runs and flag sets significant only in the full run (sample_01-dependent) vs significant in both (robust).
Report up-regulated and down-regulated sets separately; never merge directions.
If the hallmark GMT cannot be resolved from the provisioned reference data at runtime, report that failure explicitly in the step output and stop — do not silently substitute another collection.

Outputs: gsea_full.csv, gsea_reduced.csv (set, NES, pvalue, FDR, leading-edge genes), ora_results.csv, concordance table, enrichment_report.md with a top-10 summary table of robust hallmark sets (significant in both runs) including direction and leading-edge genes.
steps.description: Pathway readout: pre-ranked GSEA plus ORA against the 50 MSigDB human HALLMARK sets on both the full and shallow-sample-excluded ranked lists, with concordance flags tying pathways back to the T1S3 robustness verdict.
acceptance_criteria: gsea_full.csv and gsea_reduced.csv each cover all 50 HALLMARK sets with NES and FDR; the number of sets at FDR < 0.25 is reported per run.
ORA table is produced from de_robust.csv DE genes vs the full 12,000-gene assay background.

The concordance section identifies which significant hallmark sets are robust (both runs) vs sample_01-dependent (full run only), and the report's top-10 summary is restricted to robust sets when any exist.
ID mapping coverage is reported when the matrix is not natively HGNC-labeled.

plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: Bulk RNA-seq of human skin: 12,000 genes x 12 samples (6 treated = AD lesional, 6 control), unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene-level counts. Two issues shape the plan: (1) the record does not confirm whether the Salmon numbers are raw counts or length-corrected scaled counts — DESeq-family models assume raw counts, so QC must check the matrix (integer vs fractional) before DE; (2) sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median. Median-of-ratios size factors correct library size, but a ~5x-shallow library has sparse per-gene counts that can inflate gene-wise dispersion and create shallow-sample artifacts, so the definitive handling is a leave-out sensitivity run plus an explicit comparison, not silent exclusion. Flow: T1S1 quantifies sample_01, verifies counts/metadata agreement, ID space, and count format; T1S2 runs pydeseq2 (Python-only per user constraint) treated-vs-control with LFC shrinkage and BH FDR; T1S3 repeats the identical pipeline without sample_01 and measures how much the DE result depends on it, producing a flagged 'robust' table; T2S1 takes the full and reduced ranked lists and tests them against the 50 MSigDB human HALLMARK sets (pre-ranked GSEA + ORA), reporting concordance between the two runs so pathway claims can be made on the robust signal. All steps run in Python; no network; hallmark GMT and the NCBI human gene-identifier table are provisioned in the reference data.
